existing.description: The Vice-Chancellor's International Excellence Scholarship was established in 2015 to promote educational opportunities, foster internationalisation and support talented international applicants enrolling for the first time as new students into undergraduate or postgraduate programmes at the University of Waikato. It is worth up to NZD$15,000 towards tuition fees, is open to all areas of study, and is reviewed monthly rather than against a single annual closing date.
eligibility: Be an international student (not a New Zealand citizen or permanent resident)
Be enrolling for the first time into an undergraduate or postgraduate programme at the University of Waikato
Any area of study is eligible
existing.eligibility_summary: Open to talented international students enrolling for the first time into an undergraduate or postgraduate programme at the University of Waikato who can demonstrate excellent academic achievement. Available to all areas of study.
benefits: Up to NZD$15,000 towards tuition fees
Applies to any area of study
coverage: Up to NZD$15,000 towards tuition fees
requirements: Read the scholarship regulations before starting the application process
Complete an application to enrol at the University of Waikato first, to gain MyWaikato access
Log in to MyWaikato and open the Scholarships tab
Apply within the trimester cut-off that matches your offer of place
existing.selection_notes: The Scholarship is awarded to successful applicants who demonstrate excellent academic achievement. Applications are reviewed monthly rather than against a single annual deadline.
existing.best_fit: High-achieving international students entering an undergraduate or taught postgraduate programme at the University of Waikato for the first time.
existing.notes: Established in 2015; prior to 2023 it was named the University of Waikato International Excellence Scholarship. There is a separate, country-specific version of these regulations, which is why the record's stored official_source_url is the 'all other countries' regulations PDF.
existing.application_period: Continuous, with monthly review. Cut-offs by offer of place: 30 November (A trimester), 31 May (B trimester), 31 August (C trimester), 31 October (H or X trimester).
existing.deadline_display: No single closing date: 'This scholarship is for all areas of study and is reviewed monthly. The above closing date does not apply.' Applications must be received by 30 November for A trimester offers of place, 31 May for B trimester, 31 August for C trimester, and 31 October for H or X trimester.

scholarships.title: Vice-Chancellor's Scholarship for International Students
scholarships.official_source: University of Otago | Ōtākou Whakaihu Waka

existing.description: The University of Otago's Vice-Chancellor's Scholarship for International Students was established in 2020 to celebrate and welcome international students to the University of Otago | Ōtākou Whakaihu Waka as valued members of its community, and is awarded to support students to pursue their academic goals. It is an Entrance Scholarship worth NZD$10,000 with a one-year tenure, payable only as a credit towards tuition fees. NOTE: the stored record described a postgraduate (Masters by coursework / PGDip) scholarship; the page the stored URL pointed to now returns 404, and the only Vice-Chancellor international scholarship currently published by Otago is this undergraduate Entrance Scholarship.
eligibility: Be an international student who has completed secondary (high) school, or another approved institution granting University Entrance, overseas or within New Zealand

Be intending to enrol or already enrolled in full-time undergraduate degree-level study, or in an approved foundation diploma programme, with the objective of progressing into an undergraduate degree at the University of Otago
Intend to study at the University of Otago from 100-level (first year) through to degree
Study on campus throughout the duration of their studies
Foundation certificate programme enrollees are NOT eligible
Foundation diploma programme enrollees progressing into an undergraduate degree ARE eligible
existing.eligibility_summary: Open to all international students who have completed secondary (high) school, or study at another approved institution that grants University Entrance, either overseas or within New Zealand, and who intend to enrol or have enrolled in full-time undergraduate degree-level study, or in an approved foundation diploma programme, with the objective of progressing into an undergraduate degree at the University of Otago. Applicants must intend to study from 100-level (first year) through to degree, must study on campus throughout, and cannot be enrolling in a foundation certificate programme.
requirements: Have completed secondary school or another approved institution granting University Entrance
Be studying on campus at the University of Otago throughout

Submit through the online Entrance Scholarship application, and complete the first stages of enrolment through eVision during the Entrance Scholarship application period (1 July to 15 August) for onshore applicants
Offshore applicants must agree in their eVision study application to be considered for international scholarships
Apply within the window matching your applicant type and intended start semester
application_method: Student management system (eVision) enrolment and scholarship consideration
existing.selection_notes: The official page states 'Selection of recipients will be based upon consideration of the following factors: Academic potential, as demonstrated by programme admission.'
existing.best_fit: International secondary school leavers (or approved foundation completers) entering full-time undergraduate study at the University of Otago on campus.
existing.notes: The scholarship will only be formally awarded once, even if the applicant applies for more than one programme and receives multiple Offers of Place. Semester 2 starters receive NZD$5,000 as a tuition credit in semester 2 with the balance released in semester 1 of the following year. Deferral of the scholarship is not possible.
existing.application_period: Annual cycles with applicant-type and semester-specific windows. Offshore students: apply 1 May (year prior) to 30 April for a semester 2 start, or to 10 December for a semester 1 start. Onshore students: apply 1 July to 15 August.
existing.deadline_display: Opening dates: 1 May in the year prior to study for offshore students; 1 July for onshore students. Closing dates: 10 December for semester 1 (February) start; 30 April for semester 2 (July) start for offshore students; 15 August for onshore students.
